disclaimer ( i am not a c coder )
further research makes me believe there is an internal error in the function.
"according to AI" in cpp a function with a return type of bool on error return false what would fit what i experience.

i believe the error to occur in between line 899 - 907 in 
godot/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp

When you do not pass a `result` object then the function returns if there is any hit: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8dcf5b4eafff013b7d7022c5c1b3e33dc15e5947/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L322-L324
Otherwise it goes through more algorithms to find data for each collision, and then returns whether it detected any collisions: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8dcf5b4eafff013b7d7022c5c1b3e33dc15e5947/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L392
When you pass a `result` in the given mrp, `count == 0`. I think what is happening is the normal of the surface which is detected as colliding is orthogonal to the motion direction and the collision is being discarded: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8dcf5b4eafff013b7d7022c5c1b3e33dc15e5947/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L339-L345
After the collision I don't think the body moves any further and therefore does not hit the blue cube.

In order to fix this I think that faces with orthogonal normals to the motion direction need be allowed to count as a collider in this function?

@Kaleb-Reid 
i am not so sure about that.

you are probably right about the "orthogonal" face triggering the issue in a normal check that makes sense but

the normal check is inside a for loop that goes over all hits and "continues" when failed so it ignores the red cube (what it should) and goes to the next hit which should be blue but there seems to be no hit for blue.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8dcf5b4eafff013b7d7022c5c1b3e33dc15e5947/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L328

not sure what "hit" refers to exactly but as far as i see it for what you say to be true the normal check would need to "return" or "break" but it only "continues" and that seems right to me.

also counting the orthogonal face as hit might make it so the red cube gets returned as hit which it should not. with godot physics only the blue is returned and that is expected behavior.

not sure if what i say here is right or wrong i am not that confident in my c and physics skill.

@Kaleb-Reid 
i just build godot from source and tested your fix.
it indeed works but in the wrong way.
it returns the red box but it should return the blue box.

when switching to godot physics it returns the blue box as expected.

I fixed the discrepancy in return value [here](https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/114605), but I wouldn't integrate the fix like that.

The problem was what @Kaleb-Reid said: Without result it would early out as soon as a hit was found ignoring the fact that further down in the code hits could still be filtered out (based on normal or penetration). I've moved this logic to the collector so that the hit is filtered out earlier. The end result of this is that both versions now report no hit (while if we want to be consistent with godot physics, they should be reporting a hit against `Floor` (blue)). 

In order to fix this, the code would need a bit of an overhaul because the `JoltPhysicsDirectSpaceState3D::body_test_motion` function works roughly like this:

1. `_body_motion_cast` does a binary search along the motion to find the last fraction that is not in collision (`safe_fraction`) and the first fraction that is in collision (`unsafe_fraction`). This finds `Platform` (red) and not `Floor` as that is further away.
2. `_body_motion_collide` checks collision at the `unsafe_fraction` to return contact information of `Platform`. The [normal check](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8dcf5b4eafff013b7d7022c5c1b3e33dc15e5947/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L339-L345) inside that function causes an early out and causes the function to return `false`.
3. Now no collision is reported.

The fix would either be to do the normal filtering inside `_body_motion_cast` too or to continue looking when the `unsafe_fraction` fails to result in collision while ignoring further hits on `Platform`. I'm not going to attempt to fix this logic as it's quite delicate and @mihe spent a lot of time getting it to how it works now.
